wc:minerva-prose.summary: Typography for long-form HTML content (articles, Markdown).
wc:minerva-prose.description: Unframed, theme-aware typography for semantic HTML: articles, rendered Markdown, rich-text editor output (`<Prose>` of React). It does not parse or sanitize HTML. Why light DOM styling: the content is slotted, and shadow DOM styles can only reach slotted top-level elements (`::slotted(p)`), never their descendants (`li > code`, `table td`...). So the element injects the React library's compiled prose rules, scoped with a `minerva-prose` selector, into its root node (the document, or the shadow root it is rendered in) once per root, via `adoptedStyleSheets` (a `<style>` element where constructable stylesheets are unsupported). Injection happens on connect only, so importing the module is SSR / Node safe. The same rules are published as the React library's `prose` Sass mixin, and read the same CSS variables (`--prose-font-size`, `--prose-border-color`, ...).

Release notes

Version 2.4 brings Web Components for every primitive, sharing the design tokens of the React library. Install it with npm install.

Highlights

  • Form-associated inputs that work in a plain <form>
  • Theme scopes with <minerva-config>
    • Light, dark and system modes
    • Four palettes

Nested descendants are styled too: the rules live in the light DOM.
